intro: In this week's intelligence digest, we explore significant advancements in AI and their implications for the retail and luxury sectors, highlighted by FedEx's launch of AI-driven tracking tools and Amazon's ambitious $200 billion spending plan. Additionally, we examine the evolving landscape of consumer sentiment, as evidenced by a notable growth report from jewelers and the challenges facing the viral AI social forum, Moltbook. This week's insights underscore the intersection of technology and consumer behavior, shaping the future of commerce.

readOneThing.title: FedEx launches AI-powered tracking and returns tools

items.title: FedEx launches AI-powered tracking and returns tools
bullets: Brands using similar post-purchase engagement tools have seen 42% fewer inquiries about order status and 42% more repeat purchases.
The AI tools are now available to U.S. customers, reflecting a shift in parcel logistics towards improving the post-purchase experience.
Read the full article for details.

items.title: 58 Percent of Surveyed Jewelers Report Growth in December
bullets: 58 percent of jewelers surveyed reported sales growth in December, indicating a positive trend for the jewelry industry during the holiday season.
Only 18 percent of the 101 jewelers surveyed reported losses year over year, showcasing a relatively strong market performance.
The survey was conducted in early February 2026, reflecting sales data from December 2025 compared to the previous year.

items.title: Security concerns and scepticism are bursting the bubble of Moltbook, the viral AI social forum
bullets: Moltbook, a new social media platform for AI agents, has gained significant attention since its launch in late January 2026.
Security researchers found critical vulnerabilities on Moltbook, allowing unauthorized access to user credentials and sensitive data.
Despite concerns, over 1.6 million AI agents have registered on Moltbook, with only about 17,000 human owners identified.

items.title: Amazon’s $200 Billion Spending Plan Raises Stakes in A.I. Race
bullets: The spending plan exceeded Wall Street predictions by $50 billion, raising concerns among investors about the long-term profitability of such investments.
Amazon's announcement follows similar commitments from Google and Meta, with combined A.I. spending from major tech companies surpassing half a trillion dollars annually.
Read the full article for details.

items.title: Amazon set to pass Walmart in annual revenue for the first time after hitting $700 billion in sales
bullets: Amazon reported $716.9 billion in revenue for 2025, surpassing Walmart's expected revenue of $712 billion.
The company's cloud division, AWS, generated $35.6 billion in fourth-quarter sales, marking a 24% increase year-over-year.
Amazon's annual revenue growth follows a significant boost during the pandemic, where sales jumped 38% to $386 billion in 2020.

items.title: AI data centres could spur Internet era-type job boom, says Nvidia’s Jensen Huang
bullets: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang stated that AI infrastructure, particularly data centres, will create jobs across various sectors in India.
The Union Budget 2026 has extended tax holidays for data centre investments until 2047, potentially attracting up to $200 billion in foreign investment.
Nvidia announced a partnership with Dassault Systèmes to develop AI factories powered by its infrastructure across three continents.

items.title: Hailey Bieber’s 30-Carat Choker and 9 More Diamond Looks From the Grammys
bullets: The 2026 Grammys featured a more subdued display of celebrity diamond jewelry compared to previous years.
Hailey Bieber's standout look included a 30-carat choker and matching earrings from Lorraine Schwartz.
The event showcased various diamond pieces from renowned designers like Chopard and Cartier, appealing to a wide audience.

items.title: Cardinal Health expands ecommerce and leans on AI to boost efficiency
bullets: The company reported a 19% increase in Q2 revenue, reaching $65.6 billion, with net income rising to $467 million.
Cardinal Health aims for its biopharma services to generate $1 billion in revenue by 2028, reflecting a 30% growth within the year.
Read the full article for details.
